user.title: HA-BEMS
user.description: Choose a service entry or create an independently named operation planner. Each service entry groups its own helper or forecast registrations. Each operation planner appears as a separate integration entry.

entity_creator.title: BEMS entity creator
entity_creator.description: Create entities you don't already have in Home Assistant. Modules can also use existing entities.

thermal_storage.title: Storage duration & operation constraints
thermal_storage.description: Storage duration expresses thermal capacity as equivalent hours of full-output operation, before ongoing demand is deducted. For example, 6.4 h represents the heat produced in 6.4 operating hours; actual filling/emptying times depend on demand. The lower storage bound is always 0 h. Leave the initial value empty to start at 50% of the storage duration. Use Restart to explicitly reset the model, for example after a long outage. The feed-forward estimate is retained across restarts while its saved plan covers the current time. Changing storage or demand settings restarts the estimate. Minimum on/off times round upward to 15-minute steps and continue across replanning. The terminal storage level must remain at least the model’s initial level. Select an imported constraint forecast or an existing MILP operation plan. Direct: 1 allows operation, 0 blocks it. Inverted: 1 blocks operation, 0 allows it. For DHW to UFH, select the DHW operation plan and invert it. With no constraint selected, interpretation is ignored. {reason}

data.restart_storage_model: Restart feed-forward model from the initial storage value
data.constraint_source: Constraint forecast or MILP operation plan

soc.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
soc.description: Create a monthly seasonal SOC threshold with twelve editable percentages. If you already have a threshold entity, select it directly in FBC setup instead.

monthly.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
monthly.description:
January to December. Default values are editable suggestions based on Central European solar irradiation conditions. At or below this threshold, HA-BEMS plans to leave the battery in standard operation. For FBC, the planned charging limit equals the configured maximum charging power. Your Home Assistant automations apply the plan.

Electricity consumption varies unpredictably, and forecasts inevitably contain errors. This threshold acts as a safeguard: it reduces the flexibility available to HA-BEMS while lowering the risk of undesirable battery operation.

existing_entity.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
existing_entity.description: Select an available sensor, number or input_number containing the active threshold from 0 to 100 with unit %. Its calendar logic stays with that entity. No automatic fallback is used if it becomes unavailable.

load_profile.title: Non-flexible load profile
load_profile.description:
Estimate the non-flexible behind-the-meter building demand at 15-minute resolution. Enter annual consumption excluding separately controlled flexible loads like heat pumps, EVs, etc. Modelling is based on standard load profiles: choose H0, H25 or a constant profile throughout the year. H25 contains some average PV self-consumption influence. Select the public holiday calendar here, then choose a Bundesland or National holidays only in the next step. All fields can be changed later.

Sources: [H0 — VDEW 1999/2000 profile tables (ZIP)]({h0_source_url}); [H25 — BDEW 2025 profile tables (XLSX)]({h25_source_url}). [BDEW background and application notes]({profile_docs_url}).

fbc.title: Electrical storage management — FBC
fbc.description: FBC (Forecast based charging) provides operating plans and recommendations. Optionally consider predicted building demand by selecting a generated or imported load forecast in the next step. Each virtual device includes an FBC charging limitation enabled switch: off publishes maximum charging power for the complete plan. Use your own Home Assistant automations to apply the results to your battery system.

data.name: Virtual device
data.soc_entity: Select actual battery SOC in % used by the FBC algorithm
data.seasonal_soc_entity: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold entity

data_description.name: Name of the virtual Battery control strategy device; this does not rename your physical battery.
data_description.soc_entity: Select the measured battery state of charge, with unit % and a value from 0 to 100.
data_description.seasonal_soc_entity: If you don't already have this entity, create it using HA-BEMS: BEMS entity creator → Battery seasonal SOC min threshold.

fbc_battery.title: Battery parameters
fbc_battery.description: Use the usable (net) battery capacity corresponding to the selected SOC sensor's full 0–100% range. The efficiency is one constant factor converting forecast PV energy into stored battery energy (for example 0.95). Include the combined conversion and charging losses once. At or below the seasonal minimum SOC, the complete FBC plan allows maximum charging power.

data_description.charge_efficiency: Factor from 0 to 1: 0.95 means that 95% of forecast PV energy becomes stored battery energy. A constant factor cannot recover PV peaks already clipped in the forecast.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Enter the usable energy in kWh corresponding to a change from 0% to 100% on the selected battery SOC sensor.
data_description.target_soc_percent: SOC that FBC aims to reach by the end of the day. Keep this value aligned with the maximum SOC configured in your battery system.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Maximum charging power supported by your battery system, in W. Also used as the output limit.

fbc_forecast.title: Select FBC forecast inputs
fbc_forecast.description:
Select a registered PV AC or PV DC forecast. The choice is yours; FBC uses the selected values without converting AC/DC. Set charging efficiency to match the selected source. Optionally select a generated or imported non-flexible load forecast. With load, FBC uses max(0, PV minus load); keep both powers on a consistent basis, accounting for conversion losses outside this subtraction. AC clipping cannot be recovered by a constant efficiency. Inputs must cover the next 72 hours at 15-minute resolution. A failed selected load never silently falls back to PV only.

{reason}

data.pv_import_entry_id: PV forecast (choose AC or DC input)

data_description.load_forecast_input: Choose None for unchanged PV-only behaviour. For load-aware FBC, use building demand before PV/battery balancing; exclude battery charging. Demand above PV becomes zero available surplus; predicted battery discharge is not simulated.

fbc_preview.title: FBC forecast input tests passed

entity_importer.title: BEMS forecast importer
entity_importer.description: Register prepared forecast sensors for reuse by planning modules. Choose the forecast type; setup tests its units, values and coverage.

import_pv.title: Import PV generation forecast
import_pv.description:
Select one forecast sensor prepared in Home Assistant. Its state must be nonnegative power in W. Required attributes: schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source update time with timezone), and forecast (ordered list of start, end and power_w records). Each record must contain a timezone-aware start/end and the interval-average power in W for exactly 15 minutes. Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours without gaps, including explicit nighttime zeros. Never replace missing data with zero. A rolling helper normally needs 289 intervals. HA-BEMS tests the format and coverage before registering this input for reuse by modules. Source age is informational and does not reject an input. The original forecast remains on your source entity; the importer adds a status sensor without duplicating the forecast. [Helper design and example]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason} Choose the actual AC or DC basis of the source. Existing registrations keep working until you explicitly classify them in Configure.

data_description.forecast_entity: Use a prepared helper such as sensor.pv_generation_forecast_72h. Provider sensors must first be converted to the documented shared format.
data_description.pv_power_type: AC is inverter output; DC is PV power before conversion. Select the actual basis of your source; HA-BEMS does not convert between them.

import_preview.title: Forecast input test passed

load_region.title: Non-flexible load profile — holiday region
load_region.description: Choose the Bundesland for the selected country, or National holidays only. Regional public holidays use the Sunday load profile. This setting can be changed later.

import_load.title: Import non-flexible building load forecast
import_load.description:
Select a prepared building demand forecast sensor, before PV/battery balancing and excluding battery charging. Its state must be finite nonnegative interval-average power in W. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source update timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native list of start, end and power_w records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in ordered, contiguous 15-minute intervals. Never replace missing consumption data with zero. A rolling helper normally needs 289 intervals. Setup tests the format and coverage; source age is information only. The importer exposes input health and keeps the forecast on your source entity. Existing HA-BEMS load profiles can be selected directly in FBC without importing them. [Helper format and AI prompt]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

data_description.forecast_entity: Select a forecast of building consumption, not net grid import, measured consumption history or an energy total in kWh.

import_price.title: Import electricity import price forecast
import_price.description:
Select a prepared sensor with a finite numeric state in EUR/kWh. Use the full marginal import tariff, including applicable grid fees, taxes and VAT. Negative prices are allowed. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native ordered list of start, end and price_eur_per_kwh records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in contiguous 15-minute intervals. Source age is informational. Prepare any source conversions or predictions in your helper; HA-BEMS does not fill missing future data. The importer provides a status sensor for shared use. [Input format]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

export_price.title: Import electricity export price forecast
export_price.description:
Select a prepared sensor with a finite numeric state in EUR/kWh. Use the actual export remuneration per exported kWh. Negative remuneration is allowed. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native ordered list of start, end and price_eur_per_kwh records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in contiguous 15-minute intervals. Source age is informational. Prepare any source conversions or predictions in your helper; HA-BEMS does not fill missing future data. The importer provides a status sensor for shared use. [Input format]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

import_temperature.title: Import outdoor air temperature forecast
import_temperature.description:
Select a prepared sensor with a finite numeric state in °C. Use interval-average outdoor air temperature in degrees Celsius. Negative temperatures are allowed. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native ordered list of start, end and temperature_c records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in contiguous 15-minute intervals. Source age is informational. Prepare any source conversions or predictions in your helper; HA-BEMS does not fill missing future data. The importer provides a status sensor for shared use. [Input format]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

thermal_cost.title: Thermal runtime cost — system
thermal_cost.description: Create a named runtime-cost forecast with its own COP, nominal thermal output and forecast inputs. It publishes the current and next-72-hour costs of full 15-minute activations. Electrical demand is calculated from thermal output divided by COP.

data_description.thermal_power_kw: Nominal thermal output of the heat pump (e.g. 7 kW), or rated heat output of an electric heating element. Electrical power is this output divided by COP.
data_description.cop_model: Constant COP: e.g. a ground source heat pump, or a direct electric heating element with COP = 1. Outdoor temperature dependent COP: e.g. an air source heat pump; define 2–10 outdoor temperature/COP reference points in a lookup table for linear interpolation and extrapolation.

thermal_cop_constant.title: Constant COP
thermal_cop_constant.description: Use a positive constant COP for every interval, e.g. for a ground source heat pump or a direct electric heating element with COP = 1. No outdoor temperature forecast is required.

thermal_cop_table.title: Outdoor temperature dependent COP
thermal_cop_table.description: For an air source heat pump, select a registered outdoor temperature forecast and define 2–10 reference points in a lookup table in the next step. COP is interpolated linearly between reference points; outside their temperature range, the nearest end segment is extrapolated linearly. Missing or invalid temperatures and non-positive extrapolated COPs use your fallback COP and are flagged in the output attributes. Register a temperature source under BEMS forecast importer first.

thermal_cop_points.title: Outdoor temperature / COP lookup table
thermal_cop_points.description: Enter the selected number of reference points, one per line: outdoor temperature in °C;COP. Use a decimal dot or comma, e.g. -7;2.32 or 2;3,12. The prefilled example is based on -7 °C / 2.32, 2 °C / 3.12, 7 °C / 4.11 and 12 °C / 4.61. Adapt it to your heat pump. Additional example points are interpolated linearly. Temperatures must be unique and COPs positive. Reference points are sorted automatically.

thermal_cost_inputs.title: Thermal runtime cost — electricity inputs

data.feed_in_limit_enabled: Consider an export power limit/feed-in limitation at grid connection point
data.curtailed_price_eur_per_kwh: Price of PV above the export limit

data_description.curtailed_price_eur_per_kwh: Cost assigned to PV electricity that would otherwise be curtailed. Use 0 EUR/kWh if curtailment has no cost. Negative prices are supported.

thermal_cost_preview.title: Thermal runtime cost — preview

import_operation.title: Operation constraint forecast
import_operation.description: Select a prepared external 72-hour constraint forecast. Each record uses start, end and operation: 1 = allowed to operate; 0 = blocked. The importer preserves these values. Direct or inverted interpretation is selected in each consuming MILP setup. Existing BEMS MILP operation plans can be selected there directly, without another forecast import. {reason}

thermal_plan.title: Thermal storage management — MILP
thermal_plan.description: Create a named feed-forward thermal operation planner, e.g. DHW or UFH. Select an existing EUR/timestep cost forecast. The planner publishes an on/off recommendation and estimated storage duration for the next 72 hours. It assumes its plan is followed; no equipment feedback or device commands are used.

runtime_constant.title: Constant runtime requirement
runtime_constant.description: Enter the operating hours needed per 24 hours to cover thermal demand: 24 h/24h means always on; 12 h/24h means running half the time on average. Storage allows this runtime to shift between timesteps.

runtime_table.title: Outdoor temperature dependent runtime
runtime_table.description: Define the required runtime from outdoor temperature using 2–10 reference points. Runtime is interpolated/extrapolated linearly, then limited to the selected minimum and maximum (0–24 h/24h). An enabled heating cutoff sets demand to zero above its temperature, overriding the minimum runtime. 24 h/24h means always on; 12 h/24h means running half the time on average.

runtime_points.title: Outdoor temperature / runtime lookup table
runtime_points.description: Enter the selected number of reference points, one per line: outdoor temperature in °C;required runtime in h/24h. Decimal dots and commas are accepted. Defaults: -12.1;18 and 12;0. Runtime values must be between 0 and 24. Use your own system characteristics; minimum/maximum runtime and the optional cutoff are applied afterward.

thermal_plan_preview.title: Thermal operating plan — preview

add_planner.title: Add operation planner
add_planner.description: Create an independent integration entry for this planner.

error.invalid_entity: Choose an available numeric percentage entity from 0 to 100 with unit %.
error.self_reference: Choose an external entity; this entry cannot use its own output as its input.
error.invalid_load_profile: Check the annual consumption and the holiday country/region combination.
error.invalid_forecast: Forecast test failed. Correct the imported input or its source using the detailed message below; setup cannot continue until the test passes.
error.no_pv_import: No PV input is registered yet. Add HA-BEMS again and choose BEMS forecast importer → PV AC generation forecast or PV DC generation forecast, then complete its test.
error.invalid_thermal_settings: Check the positive thermal output/COP, nonnegative electrical power and selected temperature input.
error.invalid_cop_points: Enter exactly the selected number of reference points, one outdoor temperature;COP pair per line. Use finite numbers, unique outdoor temperatures and positive COPs. Decimal dots and commas are accepted.
error.invalid_thermal_inputs: The cost forecast could not be calculated. Check the registered inputs and details below.
error.invalid_thermal_plan: Check the runtime model, storage settings and forecast inputs.
error.invalid_runtime_points: Enter exactly the selected number of outdoor temperature;runtime pairs. Use unique temperatures and runtime values from 0 to 24 h/24h.

abort.already_configured: This service entry already exists. Open Configure on its integration entry to manage its items.

Minimum on/off times round upward to 15-minute steps and continue across replanning. The terminal storage level must remain at least the model’s initial level. Select an imported constraint forecast or an existing MILP operation plan. Direct: 1 allows operation, 0 blocks it. Inverted: 1 blocks operation, 0 allows it. For DHW to UFH, select the DHW operation plan and invert it. With no constraint selected, interpretation is ignored. {reason}

soc.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
soc.description: Create a monthly seasonal SOC threshold with twelve editable percentages. If you already have a threshold entity, select it directly in FBC setup instead.

monthly.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
monthly.description:
January to December. Default values are editable suggestions based on Central European solar irradiation conditions. At or below this threshold, HA-BEMS plans to leave the battery in standard operation. For FBC, the planned charging limit equals the configured maximum charging power. Your Home Assistant automations apply the plan.

Electricity consumption varies unpredictably, and forecasts inevitably contain errors. This threshold acts as a safeguard: it reduces the flexibility available to HA-BEMS while lowering the risk of undesirable battery operation.

existing_entity.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
existing_entity.description: Select an available sensor, number or input_number containing the active threshold from 0 to 100 with unit %. Its calendar logic stays with that entity. No automatic fallback is used if it becomes unavailable.

load_profile.title: Non-flexible load profile
load_profile.description:
Estimate the non-flexible behind-the-meter building demand at 15-minute resolution. Enter annual consumption excluding separately controlled flexible loads like heat pumps, EVs, etc. Modelling is based on standard load profiles: choose H0, H25 or a constant profile throughout the year. H25 contains some average PV self-consumption influence. Select the public holiday calendar here, then choose a Bundesland or National holidays only in the next step. All fields can be changed later.

Sources: [H0 — VDEW 1999/2000 profile tables (ZIP)]({h0_source_url}); [H25 — BDEW 2025 profile tables (XLSX)]({h25_source_url}). [BDEW background and application notes]({profile_docs_url}).

load_region.title: Non-flexible load profile — holiday region
load_region.description: Choose the Bundesland for the selected country, or National holidays only. Regional public holidays use the Sunday load profile. This setting can be changed later.

thermal_cost.title: Thermal runtime cost — system
thermal_cost.description: Create a named runtime-cost forecast with its own COP, nominal thermal output and forecast inputs. It publishes the current and next-72-hour costs of full 15-minute activations. Electrical demand is calculated from thermal output divided by COP.

data_description.thermal_power_kw: Nominal thermal output of the heat pump (e.g. 7 kW), or rated heat output of an electric heating element. Electrical power is this output divided by COP.
data_description.cop_model: Constant COP: e.g. a ground source heat pump, or a direct electric heating element with COP = 1. Outdoor temperature dependent COP: e.g. an air source heat pump; define 2–10 outdoor temperature/COP reference points in a lookup table for linear interpolation and extrapolation.

thermal_cop_constant.title: Constant COP
thermal_cop_constant.description: Use a positive constant COP for every interval, e.g. for a ground source heat pump or a direct electric heating element with COP = 1. No outdoor temperature forecast is required.

thermal_cop_table.title: Outdoor temperature dependent COP
thermal_cop_table.description: For an air source heat pump, select a registered outdoor temperature forecast and define 2–10 reference points in a lookup table in the next step. COP is interpolated linearly between reference points; outside their temperature range, the nearest end segment is extrapolated linearly. Missing or invalid temperatures and non-positive extrapolated COPs use your fallback COP and are flagged in the output attributes. Register a temperature source under BEMS forecast importer first.

thermal_cop_points.title: Outdoor temperature / COP lookup table
thermal_cop_points.description: Enter the selected number of reference points, one per line: outdoor temperature in °C;COP. Use a decimal dot or comma, e.g. -7;2.32 or 2;3,12. The prefilled example is based on -7 °C / 2.32, 2 °C / 3.12, 7 °C / 4.11 and 12 °C / 4.61. Adapt it to your heat pump. Additional example points are interpolated linearly. Temperatures must be unique and COPs positive. Reference points are sorted automatically.

data.feed_in_limit_enabled: Consider an export power limit/feed-in limitation at grid connection point
data.curtailed_price_eur_per_kwh: Price of PV above the export limit

data_description.curtailed_price_eur_per_kwh: Cost assigned to PV electricity that would otherwise be curtailed. Use 0 EUR/kWh if curtailment has no cost. Negative prices are supported.

import_pv.title: Import PV generation forecast
import_pv.description:
Select one forecast sensor prepared in Home Assistant. Its state must be nonnegative power in W. Required attributes: schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source update time with timezone), and forecast (ordered list of start, end and power_w records). Each record must contain a timezone-aware start/end and the interval-average power in W for exactly 15 minutes. Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours without gaps, including explicit nighttime zeros. Never replace missing data with zero. A rolling helper normally needs 289 intervals. HA-BEMS tests the format and coverage before registering this input for reuse by modules. Source age is informational and does not reject an input. The original forecast remains on your source entity; the importer adds a status sensor without duplicating the forecast. [Helper design and example]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason} Choose the actual AC or DC basis of the source. Existing registrations keep working until you explicitly classify them in Configure.

data_description.forecast_entity: Use a prepared helper such as sensor.pv_generation_forecast_72h. Provider sensors must first be converted to the documented shared format.
data_description.pv_power_type: AC is inverter output; DC is PV power before conversion. Select the actual basis of your source; HA-BEMS does not convert between them.

import_load.title: Import non-flexible building load forecast
import_load.description:
Select a prepared building demand forecast sensor, before PV/battery balancing and excluding battery charging. Its state must be finite nonnegative interval-average power in W. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source update timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native list of start, end and power_w records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in ordered, contiguous 15-minute intervals. Never replace missing consumption data with zero. A rolling helper normally needs 289 intervals. Setup tests the format and coverage; source age is information only. The importer exposes input health and keeps the forecast on your source entity. Existing HA-BEMS load profiles can be selected directly in FBC without importing them. [Helper format and AI prompt]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

data_description.forecast_entity: Select a forecast of building consumption, not net grid import, measured consumption history or an energy total in kWh.

import_price.title: Import electricity import price forecast
import_price.description:
Select a prepared sensor with a finite numeric state in EUR/kWh. Use the full marginal import tariff, including applicable grid fees, taxes and VAT. Negative prices are allowed. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native ordered list of start, end and price_eur_per_kwh records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in contiguous 15-minute intervals. Source age is informational. Prepare any source conversions or predictions in your helper; HA-BEMS does not fill missing future data. The importer provides a status sensor for shared use. [Input format]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

export_price.title: Import electricity export price forecast
export_price.description:
Select a prepared sensor with a finite numeric state in EUR/kWh. Use the actual export remuneration per exported kWh. Negative remuneration is allowed. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native ordered list of start, end and price_eur_per_kwh records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in contiguous 15-minute intervals. Source age is informational. Prepare any source conversions or predictions in your helper; HA-BEMS does not fill missing future data. The importer provides a status sensor for shared use. [Input format]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

import_temperature.title: Import outdoor air temperature forecast
import_temperature.description:
Select a prepared sensor with a finite numeric state in °C. Use interval-average outdoor air temperature in degrees Celsius. Negative temperatures are allowed. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native ordered list of start, end and temperature_c records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in contiguous 15-minute intervals. Source age is informational. Prepare any source conversions or predictions in your helper; HA-BEMS does not fill missing future data. The importer provides a status sensor for shared use. [Input format]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

fbc.title: Electrical storage management — FBC
fbc.description: FBC (Forecast based charging) provides operating plans and recommendations. Optionally consider predicted building demand by selecting a generated or imported load forecast in the next step. Each virtual device includes an FBC charging limitation enabled switch: off publishes maximum charging power for the complete plan. Use your own Home Assistant automations to apply the results to your battery system.

data.name: Virtual device
data.soc_entity: Select actual battery SOC in % used by the FBC algorithm
data.seasonal_soc_entity: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold entity

data_description.name: Name of the virtual Battery control strategy device; this does not rename your physical battery.
data_description.soc_entity: Select the measured battery state of charge, with unit % and a value from 0 to 100.
data_description.seasonal_soc_entity: If you don't already have this entity, create it using HA-BEMS: BEMS entity creator → Battery seasonal SOC min threshold.

fbc_battery.title: Battery parameters
fbc_battery.description: Use the usable (net) battery capacity corresponding to the selected SOC sensor's full 0–100% range. The efficiency is one constant factor converting forecast PV energy into stored battery energy (for example 0.95). Include the combined conversion and charging losses once. At or below the seasonal minimum SOC, the complete FBC plan allows maximum charging power.

data_description.charge_efficiency: Factor from 0 to 1: 0.95 means that 95% of forecast PV energy becomes stored battery energy. A constant factor cannot recover PV peaks already clipped in the forecast.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Enter the usable energy in kWh corresponding to a change from 0% to 100% on the selected battery SOC sensor.
data_description.target_soc_percent: SOC that FBC aims to reach by the end of the day. Keep this value aligned with the maximum SOC configured in your battery system.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Maximum charging power supported by your battery system, in W. Also used as the output limit.

fbc_forecast.title: Select FBC forecast inputs
fbc_forecast.description:
Select a registered PV AC or PV DC forecast. The choice is yours; FBC uses the selected values without converting AC/DC. Set charging efficiency to match the selected source. Optionally select a generated or imported non-flexible load forecast. With load, FBC uses max(0, PV minus load); keep both powers on a consistent basis, accounting for conversion losses outside this subtraction. AC clipping cannot be recovered by a constant efficiency. Inputs must cover the next 72 hours at 15-minute resolution. A failed selected load never silently falls back to PV only.

{reason}

data.pv_import_entry_id: PV forecast (choose AC or DC input)

data_description.load_forecast_input: Choose None for unchanged PV-only behaviour. For load-aware FBC, use building demand before PV/battery balancing; exclude battery charging. Demand above PV becomes zero available surplus; predicted battery discharge is not simulated.

thermal_plan.title: Thermal storage management — MILP
thermal_plan.description: Create a named feed-forward thermal operation planner, e.g. DHW or UFH. Select an existing EUR/timestep cost forecast. The planner publishes an on/off recommendation and estimated storage duration for the next 72 hours. It assumes its plan is followed; no equipment feedback or device commands are used.

runtime_constant.title: Constant runtime requirement
runtime_constant.description: Enter the operating hours needed per 24 hours to cover thermal demand: 24 h/24h means always on; 12 h/24h means running half the time on average. Storage allows this runtime to shift between timesteps.

runtime_table.title: Outdoor temperature dependent runtime
runtime_table.description: Define the required runtime from outdoor temperature using 2–10 reference points. Runtime is interpolated/extrapolated linearly, then limited to the selected minimum and maximum (0–24 h/24h). An enabled heating cutoff sets demand to zero above its temperature, overriding the minimum runtime. 24 h/24h means always on; 12 h/24h means running half the time on average.

runtime_points.title: Outdoor temperature / runtime lookup table
runtime_points.description: Enter the selected number of reference points, one per line: outdoor temperature in °C;required runtime in h/24h. Decimal dots and commas are accepted. Defaults: -12.1;18 and 12;0. Runtime values must be between 0 and 24. Use your own system characteristics; minimum/maximum runtime and the optional cutoff are applied afterward.

thermal_storage.title: Storage duration & operation constraints
thermal_storage.description: Storage duration expresses thermal capacity as equivalent hours of full-output operation, before ongoing demand is deducted. For example, 6.4 h represents the heat produced in 6.4 operating hours; actual filling/emptying times depend on demand. The lower storage bound is always 0 h. Leave the initial value empty to start at 50% of the storage duration. Use Restart to explicitly reset the model, for example after a long outage. The feed-forward estimate is retained across restarts while its saved plan covers the current time. Changing storage or demand settings restarts the estimate. Minimum on/off times round upward to 15-minute steps and continue across replanning. The terminal storage level must remain at least the model’s initial level. Select an imported constraint forecast or an existing MILP operation plan. Direct: 1 allows operation, 0 blocks it. Inverted: 1 blocks operation, 0 allows it. For DHW to UFH, select the DHW operation plan and invert it. With no constraint selected, interpretation is ignored. {reason}
